# Integrate with a third-party address verification API

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.

      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.

        if (dialog.open) {

          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
You might want to enhance the shopper experience by streamlining the process of populating and verifying the shipping address, thereby reducing the risk of user error. You can achieve this by implementing a third-party address lookup and autocomplete APIs, such as those provided by [Google Places](https://mapsplatform.google.com/maps-products/#places-section) .

This tutorial describes how to override any field in a checkout address form and extend it to integrate with this service. The implementation supports backend-configurable validation and full form submission integration.

Upon successful completion of this tutorial, a form similar to the following will be displayed:

Autocomplete shipping address
## Step-by-step

Section titled “Step-by-step”
The following steps describe how to integrate the Google Address Validation API with the Commerce boilerplate template using the provided address autocomplete implementation.

### Prerequisites

Section titled “Prerequisites”
For this tutorial, you must have a valid Google API key. [Use API keys](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/get-api-key) describes the process to obtain and set up this key.

### Download and configure the address autocomplete implementation

Section titled “Download and configure the address autocomplete implementation”
- Download the implementation: Copy the address-autocomplete.js file from /public/samples/address-autocomplete.js in this documentation repository to your project directory.
- Replace the API key placeholder: Open the address-autocomplete.js file and replace ADD-YOUR-GOOGLE-API-KEY-HERE with your actual Google API key: 1 const CONFIG = { 2 googleApiKey: 'YOUR_ACTUAL_GOOGLE_API_KEY' , 3 // ... rest of configuration 4 };

### Import and initialize the autocomplete service

Section titled “Import and initialize the autocomplete service”
In your commerce-checkout.js file, make the following changes to enable address autocomplete:

- Import the autocomplete service: 1 import { initializeAutocompleteWhenReady } from './address-autocomplete.js' ;
- Initialize the autocomplete in the initializeCheckout function: 1 const initializeCheckout = async () => { 2 // ... existing checkout initialization code ... 3 4 // Initialize address autocomplete for shipping form 5 const shippingContainer = document. querySelector ( '[data-commerce-checkout-shipping]' ); 6 if (shippingContainer) { 7 initializeAutocompleteWhenReady (shippingContainer, 'input[name="street"]' ); 8 } 9 10 // ... rest of initialization code ... 11 };

The initializeAutocompleteWhenReady function automatically:

- Waits for the address form to be rendered
- Attaches autocomplete functionality to the street input field
- Handles form field population when an address is selected
- Manages Google Maps API loading and initialization

## Example

Section titled “Example”
The complete address autocomplete implementation is available in /public/samples/address-autocomplete.js. This implementation includes:

- **AddressAutocompleteService class**: Handles Google Places API integration
- **initializeAutocompleteWhenReady function**: Utility function for easy integration
- **Automatic form field population**: Populates street, city, country, and postal code fields
- **Keyboard navigation**: Arrow keys, Enter, and Escape support
- **Error handling**: Graceful fallback when Google Maps API is unavailable

For additional customization options and advanced usage, see the implementation comments in the sample file.

Buy online, pickup in store (BOPIS) is a popular fulfillment option that allows customers to purchase items online and pick them up in-store.

The Commerce boilerplate template does not include a BOPIS checkout flow by default, but you can easily implement one using Adobe’s drop-in components.

## Step-by-step

Section titled “Step-by-step”
The following steps describe how to modify the [commerce-checkout.js](https://github.com/hlxsites/aem-boilerplate-commerce/blob/main/blocks/commerce-checkout/commerce-checkout.js) block file in the boilerplate template to allow users to choose between delivery and in-store pickup during the checkout process.

### Prerequisites

Section titled “Prerequisites”
Before you start, you must configure [in-store delivery](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/stores-sales/delivery/basic-methods/shipping-in-store-delivery) options in the Adobe Commerce Admin to define pickup locations. The [fetchPickupLocations](#fetch-pickup-locations) function retrieves the list of available pickup locations using a GraphQL query.

### Update content fragment

Section titled “Update content fragment”
- To create a new section for the delivery options, additional DOM elements are required. You can add these elements by modifying the content fragment. 1 < div class = "checkout__block checkout__delivery-method" > 2 < h2 class = "checkout__block checkout-delivery-method__title" >Delivery Method</ h2 > 3 < div class = "checkout__block checkout-delivery-method__toggle-buttons" > 4 < div class = "checkout__block checkout-delivery-method__delivery-button" ></ div > 5 < div class = "checkout__block checkout-delivery-method__in-store-pickup-button" ></ div > 6 </ div > 7 </ div > 8 < div class = "checkout__block checkout__in-store-pickup" ></ div >
- You must also add new selectors to render the required components and content. 1 const $deliveryButton = checkoutFragment. querySelector ( '.checkout-delivery-method__delivery-button' ); 2 const $inStorePickupButton = checkoutFragment. querySelector ( '. checkout-delivery-method__in-store-pickup-button' ); 3 const $inStorePickup = checkoutFragment. querySelector ( '.checkout__in-store-pickup' );

### Add toggle buttons

- Delivery
- In-store pickup

### Finalize the flow

Section titled “Finalize the flow”
After a user selects **In-store pickup** and chooses a location, the pickup form is shown, while the shipping form is hidden. This provides a clear and seamless way for users to choose how they want to receive their order.

# Implement multi-step checkout

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
This tutorial provides a customizable example to implement a comprehensive multi-step checkout in your Adobe Commerce storefront that supports **all user scenarios**: guest users, logged-in customers, and virtual products.

## Overview

Section titled “Overview”
This implementation provides a **complete multi-step checkout** for the Adobe Commerce boilerplate that handles:

- **Guest users** - Email capture and address entry
- **Logged-in customers** - Saved address selection and account integration
- **Virtual products** - Automatic shipping step bypass
- **Mixed carts** - Physical + virtual product combinations
- **Modular architecture** - Event-driven step coordination

## Implementation Features

Section titled “Implementation Features”
| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Guest users | ✅ |
| Logged-in customers | ✅ |
| Virtual products | ✅ |
| Mixed carts (physical + virtual products) | ✅ |
| Custom payment/shipping methods | 🔧 |

## Multi-step Customization

Section titled “Multi-step Customization”
Key areas specific to multi-step checkout customization:

- **Step progression logic** - Modify steps.js for custom user flows and step transitions
- **Individual step modules** - Customize step behavior in steps/ folder
- **Step validation** - Control when users can advance between steps
- **Fragment management** - Adapt step-specific HTML fragments in fragments.js
- **Step visibility** - Customize CSS classes for active/inactive step states
- **Manual synchronization** - Control when data is saved to the cart

## Architecture

Section titled “Architecture”
### File Structure

Section titled “File Structure”
The multi-step checkout implementation follows a modular architecture:

| File | Purpose | Key Features |
| --- | --- | --- |
| commerce-checkout-multi-step.js | Entry point and block decorator | Initializes the checkout system |
| commerce-checkout-multi-step.css | Step styling and visibility controls | Step progression, visual states, responsive design |
| steps.js | Main implementation | Step coordination and state management |
| steps/shipping.js | Shipping/contact step logic | Login detection, address forms, email validation |
| steps/shipping-methods.js | Delivery method selection | Shipping options, cost calculation |
| steps/payment-methods.js | Payment method selection | Payment provider integration |
| steps/billing-address.js | Billing address step | Conditional billing form rendering |
| fragments.js | HTML fragment creation | Step-specific DOM structure generation |
| containers.js | Container rendering functions | Drop-in container management |
| components.js | UI component functions | Reusable UI elements |
| utils.js | Utility functions and helpers | Virtual cart detection, validation |
| constants.js | Shared constants and configuration | CSS classes, form names, storage keys |

### Manual Synchronization Control

Section titled “Manual Synchronization Control”
In multi-step checkout, containers use **autoSync: false** to disable automatic backend synchronization, allowing manual control over when data is saved:

**AutoSync behavior:**

- **autoSync: true (default)** - Local changes automatically sync with backend via GraphQL mutations
- **autoSync: false** - Changes maintained locally only, no automatic API calls

**Why disable autoSync in multi-step:**

- **Controlled timing** - Save data only when step is completed and validated
- **Better UX** - Prevent partial/invalid data from being sent to cart
- **Step coordination** - Parent step manager controls when to persist data
- **Validation first** - Ensure all step requirements met before saving

**Manual sync example:**

```
1

2

continueFromStep
 
=
 
async
 () 
=>
 {
3
  
if
 (
!
validateStepData
()) 
return
;
4

5
  
// Manual API call with error handling
6
  
try
 {
7
    
await
 checkoutApi.
setShippingMethodsOnCart
([{
8
      
carrier_code: selectedMethod.carrier.code,
9
      
method_code: selectedMethod.code,
10
    
}]);
11
  
} 
catch
 (error) {
12
    
console.
error
(
'Failed to save step data:'
, error);
13
    
return
; 
// Don't proceed if API call fails
14
  
}
15

16
  
// Only continue if API call succeeded
17
  
await
 
displayStepSummary
(selectedMethod);
18
  
await
 
continueToNextStep
();
19

20
  
events.
emit
(
'checkout/step/completed'
, 
null
);
21
};
```

**Key patterns:**

- **Continue button trigger** - API calls happen when user clicks continue, not on selection
- **Try-catch wrapping** - All API calls must be wrapped for error handling
- **Early return on error** - If API fails, don’t proceed to next step
- **Success-only progression** - Only move forward if data successfully saved

This approach ensures data integrity and provides smooth step transitions without premature backend updates.

### API Reference

Section titled “API Reference”
Step modules rely on the checkout drop-in’s API functions for cart management. The complete API reference is available in the [Checkout functions](/developer/commerce/storefront/dropins/checkout/functions/) documentation.

**Key APIs for multi-step implementation:**

| Function | Purpose | Used In Step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| setGuestEmailOnCart() | Set guest user email | Shipping (email capture) |
| setShippingAddress() | Set shipping address on cart | Shipping (address collection) |
| setShippingMethodsOnCart() | Set shipping methods on cart | Shipping Methods |
| setPaymentMethod() | Set payment method on cart | Payment Methods |
| setBillingAddress() | Set billing address on cart | Payment Methods, Billing Address |
| isEmailAvailable() | Check email availability | Order Header (account creation) |
| getStoreConfigCache() | Get cached store configuration | Address forms (default country) |
| estimateShippingMethods() | Estimate shipping costs | Address forms (cost calculation) |

All step completion logic should use these APIs with proper error handling as shown in the manual sync examples above.

**Note:** The implementation uses event-driven data (events.lastPayload()) instead of direct getCart() or getCustomer() calls for performance optimization and real-time state management.

### Component Registry Pattern

Section titled “Component Registry Pattern”
The components.js file implements a registry system specifically for **SDK components and external UI library components**:

**Key distinction from containers:**

- **containers.js** - Manages **drop-in containers** (LoginForm, AddressForm, ShippingMethods, etc.)
- **components.js** - Manages **SDK/UI library components** (Button, Header, ProgressSpinner, etc.)

**Usage guidelines:**

- **Use components.js for:** Headers, buttons, spinners, modals, and other UI elements from the SDK
- **Use containers.js for:** Checkout drop-ins, account drop-ins, cart drop-ins, and other business logic containers
- **Recommended approach:** Keep drop-in containers and UI components in separate registries for better organization

This ensures clean architecture where components.js handles pure UI elements while containers.js manages complex business logic containers.

**Key benefits of the container system:**

- **Centralized logic** - Complex container configuration in one place
- **Prevents duplicates** - Registry ensures same container isn’t rendered multiple times
- **Memory management** - Automatic cleanup prevents memory leaks
- **State preservation** - Containers maintain state across step transitions

**Registry lifecycle:**

- **Check existing** - hasContainer() / getContainer() to find existing instances
- **Render once** - renderContainer() creates new containers only if needed
- **Cleanup** - unmountContainer() removes containers and clears references

This comprehensive container management approach ensures efficient resource usage and prevents common issues like duplicate event listeners or memory leaks.

### Create step modules

Create individual step modules that implement the universal step interface. Each step module follows the pattern described in the [Step Modules architecture section](#step-modules).

**Required step files:**

- **steps/shipping.js** - Email capture (LoginForm) and shipping address collection (AddressForm)
- **steps/shipping-methods.js** - Delivery method selection and cost calculation
- **steps/payment-methods.js** - Payment provider integration and method selection
- **steps/billing-address.js** - Conditional billing address form rendering

**Implementation reference:**

For complete implementations of these step modules, see the sample files in the [demo repository](https://github.com/hlxsites/aem-boilerplate-commerce/tree/demos/blocks/commerce-checkout-multi-step/steps) . Each file demonstrates the full step interface implementation with proper error handling, user flow logic, and integration with containers and APIs.

### Implement the steps manager

Section titled “Implement the steps manager”
Create steps.js to coordinate all step logic and manage the checkout flow. Build this step by step:

- Set up the basic structure with imports and function signature: 1 import { createShippingStep } from './steps/shipping.js' ; 2 import { createShippingMethodsStep } from './steps/shipping-methods.js' ; 3 import { createPaymentMethodsStep } from './steps/payment-methods.js' ; 4 import { createBillingAddressStep } from './steps/billing-address.js' ; 5 6 export default function createStepsManager ( block ) { 7 // Implementation will go here 8 }
- Create step instances by gathering dependencies and instantiating each step module: 1 export default function createStepsManager ( block ) { 2 const elements = getElements (block); 3 const dependencies = { elements, api, events, ui }; 4 5 const steps = { 6 shipping: createShippingStep (dependencies), 7 shippingMethods: createShippingMethodsStep (dependencies), 8 paymentMethods: createPaymentMethodsStep (dependencies), 9 billingAddress: createBillingAddressStep (dependencies) 10 }; 11 }
- Implement step coordination logic that determines which step to show based on completion status: 1 async function handleCheckoutUpdated ( data ) { 2 // Step 1: Shipping - always required 3 if ( ! steps.shipping. isComplete (data)) { 4 await steps.shipping. display (data); 5 return ; 6 } 7 await steps.shipping. displaySummary (data); 8 9 // Step 2: Shipping Methods (skip for virtual products) 10 if ( ! isVirtualCart (data)) { 11 if ( ! steps.shippingMethods. isComplete (data)) { 12 await steps.shippingMethods. display (data); 13 return ; 14 } 15 await steps.shippingMethods. displaySummary (data); 16 } 17 18 // Step 3: Payment Methods 19 if ( ! steps.paymentMethods. isComplete (data)) { 20 await steps.paymentMethods. display (data); 21 return ; 22 } 23 await steps.paymentMethods. displaySummary (data); 24 25 // Step 4: Billing Address (if needed) 26 if ( ! steps.billingAddress. isComplete (data)) { 27 await steps.billingAddress. display (data); 28 return ; 29 } 30 await steps.billingAddress. displaySummary (data); 31 }
- Wire up event handling to respond to checkout state changes: 1 return { 2 async init () { 3 events. on ( 'checkout/initialized' , handleCheckoutUpdated); 4 events. on ( 'checkout/updated' , handleCheckoutUpdated); 5 } 6 };

The steps manager uses the **early return pattern** - if a step is incomplete, it displays that step and exits. Only when all previous steps are complete does it move to the next step. This ensures proper linear progression through the checkout flow.

### Add CSS styling for step controls

Section titled “Add CSS styling for step controls”
Create the CSS that controls step visibility and progression. Add this to your commerce-checkout-multi-step.css file:

- Step visibility controls - Define the core classes that show/hide step content: 1 /* Hide all step content by default */ 2 .checkout-step-content { 3 display : none ; 4 } 5 6 /* Show content when step is active */ 7 .checkout-step-active .checkout-step-content { 8 display : block ; 9 } 10 11 /* Hide summaries by default */ 12 .checkout-step-summary { 13 display : none ; 14 } 15 16 /* Show summaries when step is completed (not active) */ 17 .checkout-step:not ( .checkout-step-active ) .checkout-step-summary { 18 display : block ; 19 } 20 21 /* Hide continue buttons when step is completed */ 22 .checkout-step:not ( .checkout-step-active ) .checkout-step-button { 23 display : none ; 24 }
- Step progression styling - For complete visual styling (borders, colors, animations, etc.), see commerce-checkout-multi-step.css in the demo repository.

These CSS rules create the core multi-step behavior: **content shows when active**, **summaries show when completed**, and **step progression controls** guide users through the checkout flow.

# Validate shipping address | Adobe Commerce Storefront

**Fonte original:** https://experienceleague.adobe.com/developer/commerce/storefront/dropins/checkout/tutorials/validate-shipping-address

# Validate shipping address

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Use the AddressValidation container to present both the original and suggested addresses from your verification service, letting shoppers choose before placing their order.

This tutorial shows how to integrate the container in the commerce-checkout block.

AddressValidation displayed in a modal
## Overview

Section titled “Overview”
At a high level:

- Call your address verification service before placing the order.
- If it returns a suggestion, open a modal and render AddressValidation.
- If the shopper selects the suggestion, persist it as the shipping address; otherwise, use the original address.

## Integration

Section titled “Integration”

# Checkout utility functions | Adobe Commerce Storefront

**Fonte original:** https://experienceleague.adobe.com/developer/commerce/storefront/dropins/checkout/utilities

# Checkout utility functions

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();

## API Functions

Section titled “API Functions”
### setAddressOnCart

Section titled “setAddressOnCart”
The setAddressOnCart function creates a debounced handler for setting shipping or billing addresses on the cart, preventing excessive API calls when address data changes frequently.

```
1
export
 
function
 
setAddressOnCart
({
2
  
type
 
=
 
'shipping'
,
3
  
debounceMs
 
=
 
0
,
4
  
placeOrderBtn
,
5
}
:
 {
6
  
type
?:
 
'shipping'
 
|
 
'billing'
;
7
  
debounceMs
?:
 
number
;
8
  
placeOrderBtn
?:
 
RenderAPI
;
9
})
:
 (
change
:
 
AddressFormChange
) 
=>
 
void
;
```

| Parameter | Type | Req? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type | string | No | Address type: "shipping" or "billing". Defaults to "shipping". |
| debounceMs | number | No | Milliseconds to debounce API calls. Defaults to 0. |
| placeOrderBtn | RenderAPI | No | Place order button API to manage disabled state. |

### Returns

Section titled “Returns”
Returns a function that accepts address form changes and updates the cart accordingly.

### Usage

Section titled “Usage”
```
1
import
 { setAddressOnCart } 
from
 
'@dropins/storefront-checkout/lib/utils.js'
;
2

3
// Set up debounced shipping address handler
4
const
 
handleShippingChange
 
=
 
setAddressOnCart
({
5
  
type: 
'shipping'
,
6
  
debounceMs: 
500
,
7
  
placeOrderBtn: placeOrderButtonAPI
8
});
9

10
// Use with form change events
11
shippingForm.
addEventListener
(
'input'
, (
event
) 
=>
 {
12
  
const
 
formData
 
=
 
getFormValues
(event.target.form);
13
  
const
 
isValid
 
=
 
validateForm
(event.target.form);
14

15
  
handleShippingChange
({
16
    
data: formData,
17
    
isDataValid: isValid
18
  
});
19
});
```

## Cart Data Functions

Section titled “Cart Data Functions”
### isVirtualCart

Section titled “isVirtualCart”
The isVirtualCart function checks if a cart contains only virtual products (no shipping required). If no argument is provided, it reads the latest checkout data.

```
1
export
 
function
 
isVirtualCart
(
data
?:
 
Cart
 
|
 
null
)
:
 
boolean
;
```

| Parameter | Type | Req? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | Cart | null | Yes | The cart data object to check. |

### Returns

Section titled “Returns”
Returns true if the cart is virtual, false otherwise.

### Usage

Section titled “Usage”
```
1
import
 { isVirtualCart } 
from
 
'@dropins/storefront-checkout/lib/utils.js'
;
2

3
// Check if shipping is required using explicit data
4
const
 
cartData
 
=
 
await
 
getCart
();
5
const
 
skipShipping
 
=
 
isVirtualCart
(cartData);
6

7
// Or check using the latest checkout data
8
const
 
skipShippingFromState
 
=
 
isVirtualCart
();
9

10
if
 (skipShipping) {
11
  
// Hide shipping-related UI
12
  
document.
querySelector
(
'.shipping-section'
).style.display 
=
 
'none'
;
13
}
```

# Order overview

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
The order drop-in component provides a comprehensive set of tools and containers designed to manage and display order-related data across various pages and scenarios. It simplifies the implementation of order management functionality and supports seamless integration with both customer accounts and guest user workflows.

Part of seller-assisted buying

The OrderStatus container labels orders placed by an administrator during an assisted session. This label belongs to the cross-drop-in [seller-assisted buying](/developer/commerce/storefront/dropins/user-account/containers/seller-assisted-buying/) feature. Read that overview first for the end-to-end flow and Admin setup.

## Architecture

Section titled “Architecture”
The order drop-in component consists of multiple containers that display order details on different pages, such as:

- Order data containers display order details within the customer account, guest user areas, and on the order confirmation page.
- Returned merchandise authorization (RMA) containers guide users through the return process and display a list of created return requests.
- The OrderSearch container enables guest users to locate their orders using a combination of email, ZIP code, and order number. This ensures easy access to order details even for users without an account. (Logged-in customers can also use this form.)

The component’s initialization process helps manage data retrieval and event emission, ensuring that containers receive the necessary data without individual fetching.

This modular architecture allows for efficient, reusable, and highly customizable implementations of order and return workflows, making it ideal for both standard and advanced e-commerce use cases. In addition, the implementation of order and return details pages includes elements such as headers, which are implemented at the boilerplate level rather than provided directly by the drop-in containers. These elements, including commerce-order-header and commerce-return-header blocks, are covered as part of the overall framework for order and return details layouts, but are distinct from the drop-in container set.

The following diagrams provide a visual composition of the order details and return details pages:

Order details containers
Return details containers
## Supported Commerce features

Section titled “Supported Commerce features”
The following table provides an overview of the Adobe Commerce guest user features that the order component supports:

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Cancel order (with email confirmation) | Supported |
| Create a return | Supported |
| Filter orders by time of purchase | Supported |
| Reorder | Supported |
| Search orders | Roadmap |
| View list of orders on the account | Supported |
| View order status | Supported |
| View return status | Supported |

## See also

Section titled “See also”
- [Seller-assisted buying](/developer/commerce/storefront/dropins/user-account/containers/seller-assisted-buying/) — extends this drop-in so the OrderStatus container labels orders placed by an administrator during an assisted session.

      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.

      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.

      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;

      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.

        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);

      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {

      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {

          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
