(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Product Recommendations displays relevant products to customers based on their browsing history and preferences, helping increase cross-selling. You must enable and configure this feature before adding it to your pages. Once configured, it displays as specific recommendation units that you can place on any page.

## Configuration

Section titled “Configuration”
Add this table to your document to configure the block:

| product-recommendations |
| --- |
| recId | *2ed7ea09-d9bd-4691-91c3-2c0a6d4fd869 (example)* |
| currentsku | *crz-eco-tr-std-2017 (example)* |
| currentprice | *49.99 (example)* |

- recId : Recommendation unit ID from the Admin. Required for all pages.
- currentsku : Seed product SKU. Required on non-PDP pages for anchor-based recommendation unit types (for example, more-like-this, visual similarity, viewed-viewed, viewed-bought, bought-bought). On PDP pages, the boilerplate reads the seed SKU automatically from the Adobe Client Data Layer (ACDL).
- currentprice : Anchor product price (numeric). Required on non-PDP pages when the unit uses dynamic or relative price filter operators (Adobe Commerce Optimizer and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service only). Not required for static price filters—a fixed price range in the filter rule does not remove the need for a seed SKU on anchor-based types. On PDP pages, the boilerplate reads anchor price automatically from ACDL when needed.

### When product context is required

Section titled “When product context is required”
Whether a seed SKU or anchor price is required depends on the **recommendation unit type** and the **price filter operator**, not on each other:

| Unit type | Seed SKU | Anchor price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anchor-based** (more-like-this, visual similarity, viewed-viewed, viewed-bought, bought-bought) | Required | Only for dynamic or relative price filter operators |
| **Context-free** (most-viewed, most-purchased, and similar popularity or behavioral types) | Not required | Not applicable |

A **static** price filter defines a fixed price range in the filter rule. It does not mean the unit can run without an anchor product. For example, a more-like-this unit with a static price filter returns no products when the seed SKU is missing, but returns results with the seed SKU alone—currentprice is not required.

### Storefront block configuration

Section titled “Storefront block configuration”
How you configure the block depends on the page type and unit type:

- **PDP pages**: Set only recId. The boilerplate supplies the seed SKU from ACDL product context. On Adobe Commerce Optimizer and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service it also sends the ACDL anchor price automatically; the backend applies it only when the unit’s filter uses a dynamic or relative operator.
- **Non-PDP pages (PLP, cart, home, and so on)**: There is no product context on these pages. For **anchor-based** unit types, you must set currentsku in block config. Add currentprice only when the unit uses dynamic or relative price filter operators (Adobe Commerce Optimizer and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service only).
- **Context-free unit types on any page**: Set only recId. These popularity and behavioral units do not use a seed product.

Important

- Do not assume recId alone is enough on non-PDP pages. That applies to **context-free** unit types only. **Anchor-based** units on non-PDP pages require currentsku or they return no products.
- Do not omit currentprice on non-PDP pages just because the unit uses a static price filter. Static filters still need a seed SKU for anchor-based types; they do not need anchor price.
- Add currentprice on non-PDP pages only when the unit’s price filter uses dynamic or relative operators.

## How to enable and configure Product Recommendations

Section titled “How to enable and configure Product Recommendations”
The Product Recommendations block can be configured on each page through Document Authoring. Follow the step-by-step guide below to enable and configure Product Recommendations:

### Create a recommendation unit

Section titled “Create a recommendation unit”
You must first create recommendation units in the Adobe Commerce Admin (PaaS) or Adobe Commerce Optimizer Admin (SaaS).

#### Adobe Commerce Optimizer Admin (SaaS)

Section titled “Adobe Commerce Optimizer Admin (SaaS)”
The following steps apply to merchants using Adobe Commerce Optimizer or Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service.

- Log in to the Adobe Commerce Optimizer Admin.
- On the Admin sidebar, go to Recommendations .
- Follow the steps in the user guide to create a recommendation unit.

Note

For Adobe Commerce Admin (PaaS), follow the steps in the [user guide](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce/product-recommendations/admin/create) to create a recommendation unit.

### Get the recommendations unit ID

Section titled “Get the recommendations unit ID”
You can specify which recommendation unit to display on each page by using the recommendation unit ID.

- Navigate to the Product Recommendations page in the Adobe Commerce Admin or Adobe Commerce Optimizer Admin.
- Click the eye icon next to the recommendation unit that you’d like to display on your store.
- Copy the Recommendation ID from the modal.

You will use this ID in the next step to configure the recommendations block.

### Add and configure the recommendations block

Section titled “Add and configure the recommendations block”
You can configure each page to display a specific recommendation unit by setting its recommendation ID.

- Open the page where you want to display the recommendation unit.
- Create a new table in your document with the block name product-recommendations . For product detail pages, set the recId to match the recommendation unit ID from the previous step. For example: product-recommendations recId 2ed7ea09-d9bd-4691-91c3-2c0a6d4fd869 Note PDP pages — set only recId for all unit types. The boilerplate reads seed SKU (and anchor price when needed) from ACDL. Non-PDP pages — anchor-based unit types — set recId and currentsku . For example, a more-like-this unit on a category page: product-recommendations recId 2ed7ea09-d9bd-4691-91c3-2c0a6d4fd869 currentsku crz-eco-tr-std-2017 This applies even when the unit uses a static price filter. The seed SKU is required; anchor price is not. Non-PDP pages — dynamic or relative price filters — also set currentprice on Adobe Commerce Optimizer or Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service: product-recommendations recId 2ed7ea09-d9bd-4691-91c3-2c0a6d4fd869 currentsku crz-eco-tr-std-2017 currentprice 49.99 Non-PDP pages — context-free unit types (most-viewed, most-purchased, and similar) — set only recId , same as on PDP.

## Section metadata

Section titled “Section metadata”
Control the section styling, spacing, and layout that wraps your commerce block. All properties are optional:

| section-metadata |
| --- |
| Style | *light (optional)* |
| Padding | *medium (optional)* |
| Margin | *small (optional)* |
| Column Width | *30% (optional)* |
| Gap | *small (optional)* |

Learn more

See the [Section Metadata guide](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/blocks/section-metadata/) for all available values and the [Page Metadata guide](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/blocks/page-metadata/) for SEO and caching options.

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
The Terms & Conditions feature must be enabled and configured to be available during the checkout process before placing an order. The configured terms and conditions will appear in the Checkout component as specific checkboxes. Each checkbox will display a label with text and links, directing users to the corresponding agreement pages configured at store-view level.

TermsAndConditions configurable on a per store-view basis

Merchants can add as many agreements as they want for a specific store-view; this allows merchants to provide different documents for each language and other needs.

Visit the [Multi-store setup](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/multistore-setup/) documentation for more information on how to build blocks and configure the storefront structure based on **Edge Delivery Services (EDS)**.

## How to enable and configure the Terms and Conditions

Section titled “How to enable and configure the Terms and Conditions”
This checkout component is configurable on a per store-view basis on EDS, but a merchant can also rely on the Admin Panel’s configuration. Follow the next step-by-step guide to enable and configure the Terms and Conditions:

### Enable the component

Section titled “Enable the component”
The merchant has to enable the component in the Admin Panel as follows:

- Log in to the Admin Panel.
- On the Admin sidebar, go to Stores > Settings > Configuration .
- In the left panel, expand Sales and choose Checkout .
- Expand the Checkout Options section.
- Set Enable Terms and Conditions to “Yes”.
- Click Save Config .

See [Terms and conditions for checkout](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/stores-sales/point-of-purchase/checkout/terms-and-conditions) documentation for more information on how to enable the terms and conditions using the Admin Panel.

### Create the agreement document

Section titled “Create the agreement document”
The agreements pages will be created **ONLY** using *document-based authoring (DBA)* within EDS instead of using the Admin Panel, allowing the merchant to create and manage as many agreements pages and content as required for each store-view and language.

### Configure the agreement checkbox label

Section titled “Configure the agreement checkbox label”
Use the **EDS placeholders** or the **Admin Panel** instructions in the following tabs to configure the agreement checkbox label.

- [Using EDS placeholders](#tab-panel-16)
- [Using the Admin Panel](#tab-panel-17)

For each agreement, the merchant has to update the **placeholders** sheet with the following information:

- An **identifier**: It’s the reference that identifies the label translated
- A **label**: It’s the text to display next to the checkbox, and will be directly retrieved from the Boilerplate translations for a specific store-view and language. This data accepts HTML with links to a specific page in EDS

Similarly, the merchant can configure the translation for the validation error that appears when the user clicks the Place Order button and an agreement is not checked, using the **“Checkout.TermsAndConditions.error”** identifier.

Sample of **placeholders** sheet:

```
1
"Checkout.TermsAndConditions.label", "I have read, understand, and accept the <a href='/en/privacy-policy' target='_blank'>Terms of Use, Terms of Sales, Privacy Policy, and Return Policy</a>."
2
"Checkout.TermsAndConditions.terms_label", "By placing an order, you are agreeing to be bound by our <a href='/en/terms-and-conditions' target='_blank'>Terms And Conditions</a>."
3
"Checkout.TermsAndConditions.privacy_label", "By placing an order, you acknowledge our <a href='/en/privacy-policy' target='_blank'>Privacy Policy</a>."
4
"Checkout.TermsAndConditions.error", "Please accept the Terms and Conditions to continue."
```

These labels are used to render the TermsAndConditions container in the **commerce-checkout.js** block file.

Refer to the Adobe Commerce documentation for examples on how to use these labels.

The merchant has to configure the checkbox label for each agreement using the Admin Panel. As mentioned before, the Admin Panel allows merchants to create configurations per store-view level as follows:

- Log in to the Admin Panel.
- On the Admin sidebar, go to Stores > Settings > Terms and Conditions .
- In the upper-right corner, click the Add New Condition button.
- Enter the following Terms and Conditions information: Condition Name The agreement identifier Status Attribute to indicate if it’s available or not: ‘Enabled’; the agreement will be retrieved by the GraphQL API query ‘Disabled’; the agreement won’t be retrieved by the GraphQL API query Applied Specifies how the checkbox should appear: ‘Manually’: the user is required to manually check and accept the conditions to place an order ‘Automatically’: the checkbox will appear checked by default, conditions are automatically accepted upon checkout Store View Defines the scope at store view level for this agreement where you want these Terms and Conditions to be used Checkbox Text It contains directly the text to show; it accepts HTML with links to a specific page in EDS Some attributes are not used Although the following attributes are provided by the Admin Panel, they are not going to be utilized in the current solution because they will be handled in EDS. Merchants are able to work on their own solution if they want to use them: Content As described above, the content for the agreements pages will be created ONLY using EDS Show Content as (Text, HTML) Not really needed because EDS pages accept HTML code Content Height (css)
- Click Save Condition . These entries are used to render the TermsAndConditions container in the commerce-checkout.js block file.

Refer to the Adobe Commerce documentation for examples of this feature.

See the [Terms and conditions for checkout](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/stores-sales/point-of-purchase/checkout/terms-and-conditions) documentation to learn how to configure the terms and conditions using the Admin Panel.

Edge Delivery Services
# Edge Delivery Services

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Edge Delivery Services is the Adobe content delivery platform that powers your Commerce storefront. It delivers fast page load speeds, high Lighthouse scores, and an authoring experience built on [Document Authoring](https://da.live) .

For your storefront, Edge Delivery Services handles content management and delivery while integrating with Adobe Commerce for product data, cart, checkout, account functionality, and more. This separation lets content authors update pages without developer involvement.

Learn more about Edge Delivery Services in the [Edge Delivery Services Overview](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/edge-delivery/overview) .

## Features for merchants

Section titled “Features for merchants”
Scheduling options
Learn about the different ways to schedule content changes, page publishing, and promotions on your storefront.
Content migration
Copy content between DA.live projects, then preview and publish on your storefront.
Redirects
Create and manage redirects using a spreadsheet so old or changed URLs still reach the right page.
Sitemaps
Learn how Edge Delivery Services generates sitemaps and how to submit them to Google Search Console.
File and content limits
File size limits for PDFs, images, videos, and documents, plus redirect and sitemap count limits.

      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));

        });

        var empty = document.createElement('p');

          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

To migrate content from one Document Authoring project to another, you use the Traverse, Import, and Bulk Operations apps. This page shows you how.

Authoring on AEM Sites instead?

This workflow is for DA.live only. For Universal Editor, see [Localization (Universal Editor)](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/quick-start/content-localization-universal-editor/).

Migrate content between Document Authoring projects.
## Before you start

Section titled “Before you start”
You’ll need:

- Write access to both projects on DA.live
- The organization and site path for each project (for example, /acme/storefront-staging and /acme/storefront)
- A target project that already exists with the right GitHub repository and Commerce backend
- Permission to preview and publish on the target, or a developer who can run Bulk Operations for you

## Step-by-step

Section titled “Step-by-step”
### Traverse the source project

Section titled “Traverse the source project”
- Open DA.live , select Apps , and open Traverse .
- Enter the source path /organization/site (for example, /acme/storefront-staging ). Start with / .
- Select Crawl , then Copy list .

Traverse your source project.
### Import into the target project

Section titled “Import into the target project”
Caution

Import overwrites any file in the target project that has the same name as a file in your list. Review your list before you run it and move any files you want to keep to a different folder in the target project so you can copy them back later as needed.

- Open Import from Apps ( da.live/apps/import ).
- Paste the file paths from the Traverse into By Url .
- In the Into field, enter your organization and target site name (for example, acme and storefront ).
- Select the Import button.

Import into the target project.
### Traverse the target project

Section titled “Traverse the target project”
- Open the Traverse app again.
- Enter the target path (for example, /acme/storefront ).
- Select the Crawl button, then the Copy list button. Use this target list in Bulk Operations, not the source list.

Traverse the target project.
### Preview and publish

Section titled “Preview and publish”
- Open the Bulk Operations app from Apps .
- Paste the target Traverse list into the URLs field.
- Choose Preview , then select Submit . Spot-check home, product list, cart, and checkout on the preview site.
- Choose Publish , then select Submit . Confirm the live site.

Preview and publish on the target site.
## Verify

Section titled “Verify”
- Open migrated content in [DA.live](https://da.live) and on the preview site.
- Spot check the home (index) page, product list page, product detail page, cart page, and checkout page.

## Reference

Section titled “Reference”
### What Import copies

Section titled “What Import copies”
The **Traverse** app lists page paths in a project. The **Import** app copies only the paths you paste from that list. A typical crawl lists storefront documents such as cart.html and checkout.html, not every image or label sheet file.

Import does not copy storefront code, Commerce catalog data, or shopper cart session data in Commerce. After Import, you still run the **Bulk Operations** app so the preview and live sites show the update.

### Images and media

Section titled “Images and media”
When you import a path, you copy the page content and the image references inside that page. Traverse does not list a top-level media folder or hidden asset folders. Add media/..., sheet, or JSON paths to your list when you need them.

If you see a broken image on the target preview site, the page references a media path (for example, /media/hero.png) that was not imported. Add that path to the Import list and run Import again, or upload the file in the target project on DA.live. See [Working with media](https://docs.da.live/authors/guides/adding-media) on docs.da.live.

### If button labels or URLs look wrong

Section titled “If button labels or URLs look wrong”
Review [placeholder sheets](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/blocks/placeholder-sheets/) (label text for cart, checkout, and other blocks) and redirects.json for URL-forwarding rules.

### Troubleshooting

Section titled “Troubleshooting”
| Symptom | What to try |
| --- | --- |
| Crawl returns nothing | Start the path with /. Confirm you have access to the project folder. |
| Import fails | Confirm access to both projects. |
| Broken images on preview | Add missing media/... paths to the Import list and import again. |
| Live site unchanged | Run **Publish** after **Preview**. |

## Related topics

Section titled “Related topics”
- [Traversing a Content Tree](https://docs.da.live/authors/guides/apps/content-tree) (docs.da.live)

      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Edge Delivery Services limits the size of files you can upload and the number of redirects and sitemap entries your site can have.

## File upload limits

Section titled “File upload limits”
Each file type you upload through [Document Authoring](https://da.live) has a maximum size. Documents and spreadsheets have the most generous limits; SVG files and favicons have much smaller ones, and any file over its limit cannot be previewed or published.

Files larger than the limit

To use a file that exceeds the limit — such as a long product demo video — ask your development team to host it on a CDN or a third-party video platform instead. You can embed or link to it from your storefront pages.

## Redirect limits

Section titled “Redirect limits”
The redirect spreadsheet has a maximum number of entries. If you are importing a large list of historical redirects, review it first and remove entries that are no longer needed.

To create or manage your redirect spreadsheet, see [Redirects](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/redirects/).

## Sitemap limits

Section titled “Sitemap limits”
Each sitemap file has a maximum URL count and file size. If your site exceeds those limits, ask your development team to split the sitemap into multiple files and create a sitemap index.

To submit your sitemap, see [Sitemaps](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/sitemaps/).

Complete limits reference

For the exact file size, redirect, and sitemap limits, see [Limits on AEM.live](https://www.aem.live/docs/limits) .

Edge Delivery Services
# Redirects

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Edge Delivery Services manages redirects through a spreadsheet, so no code changes are required.

## Redirect behavior

Section titled “Redirect behavior”
Redirects override existing pages

If you create a redirect for a URL that already has a published page, the redirect takes precedence and the page is no longer accessible at that URL. The page is not deleted. To restore page access, remove the redirect. Removing the redirect only restores access if the page is still published. If it was unpublished separately, republish it as well.

The redirect sheet matches URL paths, not query parameters. For example, /search?q=shoes and /search?q=bags both match /search. To target individual search terms, ask your developer to configure [search redirects](/developer/commerce/storefront/how-tos/search-redirects/) instead.

The redirect sheet has a maximum number of entries. If you are managing a large legacy migration, check [File and content limits](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/file-limits/) before importing historical redirects. Once your redirects are live, update your [sitemap](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/sitemaps/) so search engines find the new URLs.

## Learn more on AEM.live

Section titled “Learn more on AEM.live”
See [Redirects on AEM.live](https://www.aem.live/docs/redirects) .

Edge Delivery Services provides several ways to schedule content changes on your storefront. The right approach depends on what you’re scheduling, such as publishing a set of pages, switching promotional content, or automating recurring operations. Use the comparison table below to find the approach that fits your needs, then follow the links to get started.

Migrating from Content Staging?

If you previously used [Content Staging](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/content-design/staging/content-staging) in the Commerce Admin to schedule content updates, that feature does not apply to Edge Delivery Services storefronts. The scheduling options below are the replacements.

## Comparison

Section titled “Comparison”
| Approach | Best for | Your role | Developer role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Snapshot scheduling](#snapshot-scheduling) | Publishing pages at a specific date and time | Create snapshots, add pages, schedule publishing | One-time registration of your site with the scheduler service | Groups pages into a snapshot that publishes them together at a scheduled time. |
| [Promotion schedules](#promotion-schedules) | Turning promotions on and off by date | Author the schedule spreadsheet and content fragments | Implement the storefront code that reads the schedule | Displays different content based on the current date using a spreadsheet with start and end dates. Pages stay published. |
| [AEM Sites scheduled publishing](#aem-sites-scheduled-publishing) | Publishing content from AEM Author | Schedule publish or unpublish actions in AEM Author | None (beyond initial site setup) | Schedules publish or unpublish actions through the Manage Publication workflow in AEM Author. |
| [Recurring tasks](#recurring-tasks) | Automating index publishing, cache purges, and other repetitive operations | None | Set up GitHub Actions in the site repository | Automates Admin API calls on a cron schedule using GitHub Actions. |

Deprecated: Crontab scheduling

The original crontab-based scheduler (using a crontab sheet in the .helix folder) is **deprecated**. If you are currently using crontab scheduling, migrate to one of the approaches below based on what you used it for:

- **Publishing or unpublishing pages** → [Snapshot scheduling](#snapshot-scheduling)
- **Publishing snapshots** → [Snapshot scheduling](#snapshot-scheduling)
- **Publishing indexes** → [Recurring tasks](#recurring-tasks)
- **HTTP requests or CDN cache purges** → [Recurring tasks](#recurring-tasks)

See the [original crontab documentation](https://www.aem.live/docs/scheduling) on aem.live for reference.

## Snapshot scheduling

Section titled “Snapshot scheduling”
Use snapshot scheduling when you need to publish a set of pages together at a specific date and time. This is the recommended approach for coordinating content launches where you want to review everything before it goes live.

A **snapshot** captures the current state of one or more pages at a point in time. You add pages to a named snapshot (for example, fall-collection-2026), review the snapshot to verify everything looks correct, and then schedule it to publish. When the scheduled time arrives, all pages in the snapshot go live simultaneously.

**Common scenarios:**

- Publish a landing page, product pages, and banners together for a product launch.
- Coordinate a site-wide update where dozens of pages must go live at the same time.
- Prepare content in advance and publish it during off-hours without manual intervention.

One-time developer setup required

Before you can schedule snapshots, your developer must register your site with the snapshot scheduler service. This is a one-time setup that requires an [Admin API token](https://www.aem.live/docs/admin.html#tag/authentication) and an [Admin API key](https://www.aem.live/docs/admin-apikeys) with publish permissions.

**Get started:**

- **Document Authoring (da.live):** See the [DA Snapshots guide](https://docs.da.live/authors/guides/apps/snapshots) for creating, managing, and scheduling snapshots.
- **SharePoint or Google Drive:** Use the [Snapshot Admin tool](https://tools.aem.live/tools/snapshot-admin/index.html) to manage snapshots and schedule them for publishing.
- **All authoring methods:** See [Snapshots and Reviews](https://www.aem.live/docs/snapshots-reviews) on aem.live for the full lifecycle, including review environments and approval workflows.

## Promotion schedules

Section titled “Promotion schedules”
Use promotion schedules when you want to rotate time-sensitive content — like sale banners or seasonal campaigns — on and off based on dates you define. Unlike snapshot scheduling, this approach does **not** publish or unpublish pages. Instead, it displays different content fragments on already-published pages based on the current date and time.

**What you do:** Author a schedule spreadsheet with start dates, end dates, and links to content fragments for each promotion. A default entry (with no dates) serves as the fallback when no promotion is active. You also author the content fragments for each promotion.

**What your developer does:** Implement the storefront code that reads the published schedule and displays the correct content fragment based on the current date.

**Common scenarios:**

- Display a “4th of July Sale” banner only during the holiday week.
- Rotate seasonal promotions (Memorial Day, Back to School, Halloween) throughout the year.
- Show different hero content or calls-to-action based on an active campaign window.

Preview future promotions

You can preview what your site will look like during a future promotion by appending a schedule parameter to your pre-production URL. For example: https://main--{your-site}--{your-org}.aem.live/?schedule={timestamp}. Do not expose your production promotion data publicly if it contains confidential campaign details.

**Get started:** Work with your developer to implement promotion schedules for your storefront. The overview above describes the spreadsheet structure and content fragment approach your developer needs to build.

## AEM Sites scheduled publishing

Section titled “AEM Sites scheduled publishing”
Use AEM Sites scheduled publishing when you author content in **AEM Sites (WYSIWYG)** with AEM as a Cloud Service. This approach uses the **Manage Publication** workflow in AEM Author to schedule publish or unpublish actions for a specific date and time. Once AEM publishes the content, the changes go live on Edge Delivery Services automatically.

AEM Sites authoring only

This approach only works with AEM Sites (WYSIWYG) authoring. It does **not** apply to document-based authoring with DA, SharePoint, or Google Drive. For document-based authoring, use [snapshot scheduling](#snapshot-scheduling) or [promotion schedules](#promotion-schedules) instead.

**Get started:**

- [Publishing Pages](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/sites/authoring/sites-console/publishing-pages) — Experience League guide with detailed instructions on scheduling publish and unpublish actions.

## Recurring tasks

Section titled “Recurring tasks”
Use recurring tasks to automate repetitive operations on a schedule, such as publishing an index or purging CDN caches. This is a developer-managed approach that replaces the publish-index, http, and similar commands from the deprecated crontab scheduler.

**What your developer does:** Create a GitHub Action in the site repository that calls the AEM Admin API on a cron schedule. No merchant involvement is needed after the initial setup.

**Common scenarios:**

- Publish a query index every hour to keep search results current.
- Automate periodic cache purges for frequently updated content.

**Get started:**

- [Schedule recurring tasks](https://www.aem.live/docs/recurring) — Step-by-step example using GitHub Actions on aem.live.
- [Admin API keys](https://www.aem.live/docs/admin-apikeys) — Required for authenticating automated requests to the Admin API.

# Sitemaps | Adobe Commerce Storefront

**Fonte original:** https://experienceleague.adobe.com/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/sitemaps

**Coletado em (UTC):** 2026-07-22T14:27:58.993541+00:00

---

Edge Delivery Services
# Sitemaps

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Edge Delivery Services automatically generates a sitemap at /sitemap.xml when you publish content, so no extra setup is required.

## What gets included automatically

Section titled “What gets included automatically”
Every page you publish appears in the sitemap, including marketing pages, landing pages, authored category pages, and other document-based content.

Product pages are excluded by default. If your developer has configured [AEM Commerce prerender](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/aem-prerender/), it publishes each product page and updates the sitemap automatically. Otherwise, ask your developer to include them.

## Submit your sitemap to Google Search Console

Section titled “Submit your sitemap to Google Search Console”
In [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console) , open the **Sitemaps** section for your property, enter your sitemap URL (typically https://www.yoursite.com/sitemap.xml), and choose **Submit**. Google starts crawling the submitted URLs within a few days. Check indexing status and errors in Search Console.

Multiple sitemaps

Large catalogs or multi-language sites can have more than one sitemap file. Ask your developer to give you the complete list of sitemap URLs, then submit each one to Google Search Console.

## When to involve a developer

Section titled “When to involve a developer”
For most storefronts, the automatic sitemap is enough. Contact your developer if any of the following apply:

- Your site supports multiple languages and search engines are indexing the wrong locale.
- Your catalog has grown large enough that a single sitemap file cannot hold all product URLs. See [File and content limits](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/file-limits/) for the per-file limits.
- You need custom configuration such as hreflang tags for a multi-store setup.

If you restructured your URLs, set up [Redirects](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/edge-delivery-services/redirects/) to preserve SEO value from the old paths.

See [Sitemaps on AEM.live](https://www.aem.live/developer/sitemap) .
