The following recv snippet has the following purpose:

- Path-based routing for Edge Delivery Services, Catalog Service, and Adobe Commerce backends
- Preparing the requests for the respective backends
- Blocking access to non-production environments (non-production environments should not be indexed by search engines)

**Type**: recv

**Priority**: 100

```
1
unset req.http.x-commerce;
2

3
# Catalog Service
4
if (req.url.path ~ "^/cs-graphql$") {
5
    
# Disable Commerce WAF as it can interfere with some queries
6
    
set req.http.bypasswaf = "true";
7

8
    
# Forward to Catalog Service GraphQL
9
    
set req.backend = F_catalog_service;
10
    
set req.http.host = "catalog-service.adobe.io";
11
    
set req.url = regsub(req.url, "^/cs-graphql", "/graphql");
12

13
    
# Remove cookies
14
    
unset req.http.Cookie;
15
}
16
else if (req.url.path ~ "^/(graphql|rest|oauth|media|checkout|customer|admin|static)($|/)") {
17
    
# Commerce routes, e.g. for product images, core GQL/Rest, Luma Bridge (any paths which should load Commerce origin)
18
    
set req.backend = F_commerce;
19
    
set req.http.x-commerce = "true";
20
}
21
else
22
{
23
    
# Block access to non-prod configs
24
    
if (req.url ~ "^/configs-(stage|dev)\.json$") {
25
        
error 404 "Not Found";
26
    
}
27

28
    
# Everything else is considered Edge Delivery Services
29
    
set req.backend = F_edge_delivery;
30
    
# Restore accepted encoding
31
    
set req.http.Accept-Encoding = req.http.Fastly-Orig-Accept-Encoding;
32
    
if (req.url.path !~ "/media_[0-9a-f]{40,}[/a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\.[0-9a-z]+$"
33
        
&& req.url.ext !~ "(?i)^(gif|png|jpe?g|webp)$"
34
        
&& req.url.ext != "json"
35
        
&& req.url.path != "/.auth") {
36
        
# trim the query string to improve caching
37
        
set req.url = req.url.path;
38
        
# replace some special characters with a dash because Edge doesn't support them
39
        
set req.url = regsuball(req.url, "[()]", "-");
40

41
    
}
42
}
```

### pass

Section titled “pass”
In the pass snippet, we set the correct host URL to fetch from depending on the backend that was selected in the recv snippet.

If it’s not a request to Adobe Commerce, we skip (return pass will invoke fetch) the rest of the default pass VCL.

**Type**: pass

**Priority**: 30

```
1
if (req.backend == F_edge_delivery) {
2
    
set bereq.http.Host = "main--aem-boilerplate-commerce--hlxsites.aem.live";
3
    
set bereq.http.X-BYO-CDN-Type = "fastly";
4
    
set bereq.http.X-Push-Invalidation = "enabled";
5
}
6

7
if (!req.http.x-commerce) {
8
    
return(pass);
9
}
```

Note

Changes to the host header set here will require a Commerce Fastly cache purge due to [how and when Fastly calculates cache HITS](https://docs.fastly.com/en/guides/manipulating-the-cache-key#redefining-the-cache-key) .

### miss

Section titled “miss”
Same as pass.

**Type**: miss

**Priority**: 30

```
1
if (req.backend == F_edge_delivery) {
2
    
set bereq.http.Host = "main--aem-boilerplate-commerce--hlxsites.aem.live";
3
    
set bereq.http.X-BYO-CDN-Type = "fastly";
4
    
set bereq.http.X-Push-Invalidation = "enabled";
5
}
6

7
if (!req.http.x-commerce) {
8
    
return(fetch);
9
}
```

Note

Changes to the Host header set here will require a Commerce Fastly cache purge due to [how and when Fastly calculates cache HITS](https://docs.fastly.com/en/guides/manipulating-the-cache-key#redefining-the-cache-key) .

### fetch

Section titled “fetch”
If fetching from a backend other than Adobe Commerce, skip the rest of the [default deliver VCL](https://github.com/fastly/fastly-magento2/blob/fdd616cd0f945530e02e92e594ca00fd7990f557/etc/vcl_snippets/fetch.vcl) because this is only relevant to Adobe Commerce backends.

**Type**: fetch

**Priority**: 30

```
1
if (!req.http.x-commerce) {
2
    
unset beresp.http.Set-Cookie;
3
    
return(deliver);
4
}
```

### deliver

Section titled “deliver”
This comes from the Edge Delivery Services [Fastly setup](https://www.aem.live/docs/byo-cdn-fastly-setup#:~:text=Finally%20create%20a%20deliver%20snippet) .

**Type**: deliver

**Priority**: 30

```
1
if (req.backend == F_edge_delivery) {
2
    
unset resp.http.Age;
3

4
    
if (req.url.path !~ "\.plain\.html$") {
5
        
unset resp.http.X-Robots-Tag;
6
    
}
7
}
```

## Optional configuration

Section titled “Optional configuration”
The following are optional configurations that can be added to the VCL snippets to handle specific use cases.

### URL rewrites

Section titled “URL rewrites”
Be aware that URLs in Edge Delivery Services can only contain a-z, 0-9, and the dash (-) character (see [Document naming restrictions](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/seo/platform-limits/#document-naming-and-url-format)). You might need to create a CDN rule to rewrite or remove these characters.

As an example, consider one possible case where this applies with login referrer links. Luma may redirect to a page like /login/referrer/<base64string>. If the login page is implemented in Edge Delivery Services (with a Luma Bridge) and the base 64 string contains unsupported characters, this page will 404. Since the base64 part is only needed on the Edge Delivery Services client side to handle redirecting after a successful sign-in, this could be stripped for the request to the Edge Delivery Services backend.

Note

The exact cases where this needs to be performed, and the steps required, depend on the implementation of the Luma Bridge as well as customizations of Adobe Commerce.

### GeoIP

Section titled “GeoIP”
The following example redirects users to a country-specific path based on their IP address. It uses the country_to_store table, which is a built-in Fastly table that maps country codes to store codes. You must install the Fastly CDN [extension](https://commercemarketplace.adobe.com/fastly-magento2.html) or [module](https://github.com/fastly/fastly-magento2) to use this example.

Add the following to the recv snippet:

```
1
# Enable the GeoIP feature, allowing the VCL to use GeoIP data for various purposes, such as redirecting users based on their geographic location.
2

3
pragma optional_param geoip_opt_in true;
4

5
# Snippet GeoIpRedirect
6
 
declare local var.countryCode STRING;
7

8
# Only apply redirection if the URL has no country-specific path
9

10
# This snippet performs a GeoIP-based redirection. It checks if the request is made to the
11
# "example.com" domain and if the URL path is either the root ("/") or empty. If these conditions are met, it
12
# retrieves the user's country code based on their IP address using the `client.geo.country_code` variable.
13
# It then looks up the corresponding store code from the `country_to_store` table. The user is redirected
14
# to the appropriate country-specific URL.
15

16
if ((req.http.host ~ "example.com") && ((req.url.path == "/") || (req.url.path == "")))  {
17
      
# Retrieve the user's country based on IP address
18
      
set var.countryCode = table.lookup(country_to_store, client.geo.country_code,"us");
19
      
set req.http.X-Redirect-Url = "https://" + req.http.host + "/" + var.countryCode;
20
      
if (req.url.qs != "") {
21
                   
set req.http.X-Redirect-Url = req.http.X-Redirect-Url + "?" + req.url.qs;
22
      
}
23
        
error 701;
24
   
}
25
# End of Snippet GeoIpRedirect
26

27
# This table maps country codes to store codes. It is used in the GeoIP redirect logic to determine
28
# the appropriate store URL based on the user's geographic location.
29

30
table country_to_store {
31
    
"FR": "fr",
32
    
"AU": "au",
33
    
"NZ": "nz",
34
    
"CA": "ca",
35
    
...
36
}
```

### Proxy RUM through the origin to avoid a TLS handshake

Section titled “Proxy RUM through the origin to avoid a TLS handshake”
Add a new backend called hlx_rum that points to rum.hlx.page. Also, change the [Real Use Monitoring (RUM)](https://www.aem.live/docs/rum) implementation in aem.js to use a relative path to the origin instead of rum.hlx.page.

Add the following to the recv snippet:

```
1
if (req.url.path ~ "^/\.rum/") {
2
    
# AEM Real User Monitoring
3
    
set req.backend = F_hlx_rum;
4
    
unset req.http.Cookie;
5
}
```

### Shielding

Section titled “Shielding”
If you enable shielding in a backend, then conditions like req.backend == F_commerce may not work. For this reason, the snippets above use a header like http.x-commerce that is set/unset, which is then used instead of the direct backend variable.

### Compression

Section titled “Compression”
In fetch, you can add compression for non-Adobe Commerce resources by adding this snippet to the fetch VCL:

```
1
if (!req.http.x-commerce) {
2
    
unset beresp.http.Set-Cookie;
3
    
if (beresp.http.content-type ~ "(text/|/json|/javascript)") {
4
        
if (!beresp.http.Vary ~ "Accept-Encoding") {
5
            
set beresp.http.Vary:Accept-Encoding = "";
6
        
}
7
        
if (req.http.Accept-Encoding == "br") {
8
            
set beresp.brotli = true;
9
        
} else if (req.http.Accept-Encoding == "gzip") {
10
            
set beresp.gzip = true;
11
        
}
12
    
}
13
    
return(deliver);
14
}
```

Since the deliver VCL skips all the subsequent steps, the default compression settings are skipped. The snippet above is the same as in the default VCL, but copied again to be applied to responses that are not going to the Adobe Commerce backend.

### Failover

Section titled “Failover”
We can support automatic failover from Edge Delivery Services to Adobe Commerce Luma pages on a 404 in Edge Delivery Services. To do this, add the following in your custom fetch snippet:

```
1
if (req.backend == F_edge && http_status_matches(beresp.status, "404")) {
2
      
# See <https://www.fastly.com/documentation/solutions/examples/failover-to-a-secondary-backend/>
3
      
set beresp.http.Vary:restarts = ""; # Add restart to vary key
4
      
set beresp.cacheable = true; # Errors are not cacheable by default, so enable them
5
      
set beresp.ttl = 5s; # Set a short ttl so the unfindable object expires quickly
6
      
set beresp.http.do_failover = "yes";
7
   
}
```

Then, in your custom recv snippet:

```
1
if (req.http.try-alt-origin) {
2
    
set req.backend = F_commerce;
3
    
set req.http.x-commerce = "true";
4
    
set req.http.restarts = req.restarts; # Use restart value for vary key
5
    
set req.http.Fastly-Force-Shield = "1";
6
}
```

Factly-Force-Shield may be required to turn on clustering (not related to shielding despite the name).

Flow of EDS request: In recv, hits Edge Delivery Services case, then goes to miss, then goes to fetch, fetch returns 404 and sets retry (as snippet above), and deliver calls restart.

If we are using Fastly shielding, we need to have fastly.ff.visits_this_service == 0 in the deliver snippet, before restart, otherwise it can be that ESI doesn’t work.

```
1
if (fastly.ff.visits_this_service == 0 && !req.http.try-alt-origin && resp.http.do_failover == "yes") {
2
    
set req.http.try-alt-origin = "1";
3
    
set req.url = req.http.Magento-Original-URL;
4
    
return (restart);
5
}
```

It is not recommended to handle all paths that need to be routed to Luma like this, but still hardcode those that are known, in order to reduce load of 404s on Edge Delivery Services.

### API Mesh

Section titled “API Mesh”
API Mesh has a header size limit. You must remove third-party cookies if you’re using API mesh. Add this in the graphql section of recv snippet:

```
1
if (req.http.Cookie) {
2
        
# Remove all 3rd-party cookies
3
        
# API Mesh has a header size limit
4
        
set req.http.Cookie = ";" + req.http.Cookie;
5
        
set req.http.Cookie = regsuball(req.http.Cookie, "; +", ";");
6
        
set req.http.Cookie = regsuball(req.http.Cookie, ";(PHPSESSID|X-Magento-Vary|form_key|private_content_version|mage-messages|persistent_shopping_cart|fastly_geo_store)=", "; \\1=");
7
        
set req.http.Cookie = regsuball(req.http.Cookie, ";[^ ][^;]*", "");
8
        
set req.http.Cookie = regsuball(req.http.Cookie, "^[; ]+|[; ]+$", "");
9
        
if (req.http.cookie ~ "^\\s*$") {
10
            
unset req.http.cookie;
11
        
}
12
    
}
```

### Branch names on staging

Section titled “Branch names on staging”
You can enable the use of Edge Delivery Services branches on a staging URL (for example, branch1.my-staging.com). Use regex to get the domain name with this addition to the miss snippet:

```
1
if (req.backend == F_edge) {
2
    
if (req.http.Host ~ "^([^.]+)\\.([^.]+)\\.example\\.com$") {
3
        
set bereq.http.Host = re.group.1 + "--your-eds-url.aem.page";
4
    
} else {
5
        
set bereq.http.Host = "your-eds-url.aem.live";
6
    
}
7
    
set bereq.http.X-BYO-CDN-Type = "fastly";
8
    
set bereq.http.X-Push-Invalidation = "enabled";
9
}
```

In the domains configuration, you must use a wildcard. Since the Commerce Admin doesn’t let you do this, you must do it using the Fastly CLI (which also shows the wildcard URL in the Admin).

### Maintenance mode

Section titled “Maintenance mode”
The storefront has no built-in maintenance mode. However, you can add a custom VCL snippet similar to the one below to redirect all incoming requests to your maintenance page. This snippet excludes requests to the /maintenance path, so the maintenance page itself stays reachable.

```
1
if (req.url !~ "^/maintenance") {
2
  
error 302 "https://yoursite.com/maintenance";
3
}
```

The error 302 instruction issues an HTTP 302 (temporary redirect) to the URL you specify. Replace https://yoursite.com/maintenance with the URL of your maintenance page. Add this as a recv snippet with a priority lower than 100, for example 5, so it runs before the main routing logic.

To add the snippet, see [Getting started with custom VCL](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-cloud-service/user-guide/cdn/custom-vcl-snippets/fastly-vcl-custom-snippets) in the Fastly documentation, or use the [fastly-magento2](https://github.com/fastly/fastly-magento2) Admin module in the Commerce Admin. Work with your Fastly administrator to confirm the priority before applying the snippet.

API and GraphQL traffic

This redirect applies to all incoming requests, including GraphQL and API Mesh requests.

To end maintenance mode, remove or disable the snippet in your Fastly configuration.

### Multiple set-cookie headers workaround

Section titled “Multiple set-cookie headers workaround”
There’s a known issue with multiple set-cookie headers in API Mesh. See the following snippet for a workaround

```
1
if (req.http.x-mesh == "true") {
2
    
# There's a bug in API MESH that combines multiple set-cookie headers
3
    
# Let's remove these cookies from the response
4
    
declare local var.ignored BOOL;
5
    
set var.ignored = setcookie.delete_by_name(beresp, "private_content_version");
6
    
set var.ignored = setcookie.delete_by_name(beresp, "form_key");
7
    
set var.ignored = setcookie.delete_by_name(beresp, "authentication_flag");
8
    
set var.ignored = setcookie.delete_by_name(beresp, "dataservices_customer_id");
9
    
set var.ignored = setcookie.delete_by_name(beresp, "dataservices_customer_group");
10
    
set var.ignored = setcookie.delete_by_name(beresp, "dataservices_cart_id");
11
    
return (pass);
12
}
```

Note

x-mesh header is just an example. It would be added in API Mesh to use as determination in routing of VCL (for example, x-commerce-bypass-fastly-cache).

## Commerce configuration

Section titled “Commerce configuration”
If you are using the VCL to do the APEX redirect (aemshop.net → www.aemshop.net with 801 error), you should do two things in the Adobe Commerce backend:

- Disable auto-redirect.
- Set the base_url and secure_base_url settings to your domain, including www.

Follow these steps:

- Log in to the Adobe Commerce Admin.
- Click Stores > Settings > Configuration > General > Web .
- Expand the URL options section.
- Set Auto-redirect to Base URL to No .
- Expand the Base URLs section.
- Set the Base URL and Secure Base URL to your domain, including www . For example: https://www.aemshop.net/
- Expand the Base URLs (Secure) section.
- Set the Secure Base URL to your domain, including www . For example: https://www.aemshop.net/
- Click Save Config .

## Edge Delivery Service configuration

Section titled “Edge Delivery Service configuration”
To obtain a purge API token for Fastly, you must contact Adobe Commerce Customer Support.

Then, follow the instructions in [Setup push invalidation for Fastly](https://www.aem.live/docs/byo-cdn-fastly-setup#setup-push-invalidation-for-fastly) . The remaining configuration described on this page is already taken care of by applying the VCL snippets above.

## Validation

Section titled “Validation”
To validate your CDN setup, use curl requests to check expected responses from the paths you have configured.

### Content encoding, surrogate key, and cache

Section titled “Content encoding, surrogate key, and cache”
Validate that surrogate key, cache hits, and content encoding are working as expected by requesting an Edge Delivery Services-served asset from your Commerce domain. Ensure you are checking a warm cache by making the request at least twice. The following examples are to a warmed cache.

Here is an example of validation against an Adobe staging environment:

```
1
curl
 
-sI
 
-H
 
'Fastly-Debug: 1'
 
https://www.aemshop.net/scripts/aem.js
 
|
 
grep
 
'x-cache\|surrogate-key\|cache-control'
```

```
1
content-encoding: gzip
2
surrogate-key: develop--aem-boilerplate-commerce--hlxsites develop--aem-boilerplate-commerce--hlxsites_code E3hjdgev7F5OyPUD
3
x-cache: MISS, HIT, HIT, HIT
4
x-cache-hits: 0, 37, 1, 0
```

- content-encoding : Should be gzip or br for things like JS assets and HTML files, which should be encoded from origin.
- surrogate-key : Should not be text . If the value is text , make sure you have correctly configured the fetch VCL snippet to return deliver for Edge Delivery Servicespaths. The reason for this validation step is that the default Commerce Fastly VCL sets this. This overwrites the Edge Delivery Services surrogate key, which is required for cache invalidation to work correctly when a page is re-published.
- x-cache : Should contain HIT entries. The last entry should be HIT ( MISS , HIT , MISS , HIT ) is ok.

Also, make sure that you validate gzip encoding is applied to HTML pages:

```
1
curl
 
-sI
 
-H
 
'accept-encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd'
 
https://www.aemshop.net
 
|
 
grep
 
content-encoding
```

```
1
content-encoding: gzip
```

```
1
curl
 
-sI
 
-H
 
'accept-encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd'
 
https://www.aemshop.net/index.plain.html
 
|
 
grep
 
content-encoding
```

```
1
content-encoding: gzip
```

Validate the CDN configuration with the BYOCDN [push invalidator tool](https://tools.aem.live/) . Additionally, preview and publish a document and validate that the changes are correctly reflected.

```
1
curl
 
-Is
 
--http2
 
https://www.aemshop.net
 
|
 
grep
 
'HTTP/2'
```

```
1
HTTP/2 200
```

Validate that all requests are using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connections.

```
1
curl
 
-Is
 
-L
 
https://aemshop.net
 
|
 
grep
 
location
```

```
1
location: https://www.aemshop.net/
```

To validate the APEX redirect, observe the location header returned by a request to the domain without www.

### Image optimization

Section titled “Image optimization”
Validate that images are encoded with the expected format. If you get back image/jpeg this indicates an issue, probably Commerce Fastly is rewriting the content type header. You’ll need to validate the VCL snippets.

To validate Edge Delivery Services, ensure you check some content expected to be served from the Edge Delivery Services origin (such as the hero banner).

```
1
curl
 
-sI
 
-H
 
"Accept: image/webp"
 
'https://www.aemshop.net/media_1b6ab8fa5166c1d9ab57a109f4f97b8e950a3ed84.png?width=2000&format=webply&optimize=medium'
 
|
 
grep
 
'content-type'
```

```
1
content-type: image/webp
```

To validate Commerce, ensure you check some content expected to be served from the Adobe Commerce origin (such as a product image).

```
1
curl
 
-sI
  
-H
 
"Accept: image/webp"
 
'https://www.aemshop.net/media/catalog/product/adobestoredata/ADB150.jpg?auto=webp&quality=80&crop=false&fit=cover&width=960&height=1191'
 
|
 
grep
 
'content-type'
```

```
1
content-type: image/webp
```

### Commerce cache

Section titled “Commerce cache”
Ensure that GraphQL GET requests result in cache HITs.

```
1
curl
 
-sI
 
'https://www.aemshop.net/graphql?query=query+STORE_CONFIG_QUERY+%7B+storeConfig+%7B+minicart_display%7D+%7D'
 
|
 
grep
 
x-cache
```

```
1
x-cache: HIT
2
x-cache-hits: 1
```

### Commerce base URL

Section titled “Commerce base URL”
Ensure that the base URL change is propagated to Catalog Service. You can do this with a query against your Catalog Service API to verify that the URLs for product images contain the APEX domain, including www. This is to prevent a redirect and subsequent load for images not including the APEX domain.

## Troubleshooting

Section titled “Troubleshooting”
It's confusing - we get it

Fastly VCL and CDN configuration can be a bit overwhelming at first. Here’s a collection of troubleshooting steps that might help you if you have problems.

### Fastly API quick reference

Section titled “Fastly API quick reference”
With your Fastly API Token you can make requests against the Fastly API for information or data that may be otherwise inaccessible. You can find your API Token in your Commerce Admin view under **Stores** > **Settings** > **Configuration** > **Advanced** > **System** > **Full Page Cache** > **Fastly Configuration**.

Here’s a quick reference of things you can do with your API Token. See [Fastly's API documentation](https://www.fastly.com/documentation/reference/api/) for more details.

```
1
# retrieve active version
2
curl
 
-H
 
"Fastly-Key: API_TOKEN"
 
"https://api.fastly.com/service/SERVICE_ID/version"
3

4
# retrieve full, generated VCL
5
curl
 
-H
 
"Fastly-Key: API_TOKEN"
 
"https://api.fastly.com/service/SERVICE_ID/version/VERSION/generated_vcl"
6

7
# retrieve all snippets
8
curl
 
-H
 
"Fastly-Key: API_TOKEN"
 
"https://api.fastly.com/service/SERVICE_ID/version/VERSION/snippet"
```

### Missing snippets

Section titled “Missing snippets”
Fastly maintains a “version” of your snippets remotely on their servers. These versions are never pulled “down” to your Commerce environment, but can be “pushed” from your environment to Fastly. Unintentional local changes can cause things to become out of sync.

For example, renaming a snippet actually creates a new snippet with the new name, and does not delete the old one. You should not rename snippets unless you must. See [this issue](https://github.com/fastly/fastly-magento2/issues/708) for more information.

Your environment stores custom VCL snippets in the var/vcl_snippets_custom/ directory. If you delete that directory or its contents, you will not be able to view, edit, or modify the snippets, even though they remain active in Fastly.”

To resolve this, you should use the Fastly API to “pull” all snippets and then place them back in that folder (with permission **775**). The following table details how to construct the file correctly:

| var directory filename | Admin Panel Field | Fastly Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *recv_100_snippetrecv.vcl* | Type: *recv* Priority: *100* Name: *snippetrecv* | Type: *recv* Priority: *100* Name: *magentomodule_snippetrecv* |

# CORS Setup | Adobe Commerce Storefront

**Fonte original:** https://experienceleague.adobe.com/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/cors-setup

**Coletado em (UTC):** 2026-07-22T14:23:37.208310+00:00

---

# CORS Setup

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {

        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is a browser security feature that restricts web pages from making requests to a different domain than the one serving the page. CORS is required when your storefront runs on a different domain or port than your Adobe Commerce backend.

PaaS only
Production recommendation

CORS should be a last resort for production. Prefer same-origin delivery of the storefront and API (for example, via Fastly VCL) to avoid CORS entirely.

But during development, it’s a common scenario for storefronts to run on a different domain or port than the Adobe Commerce backend, so CORS is required. Without CORS, browsers will block cross-origin requests and you’ll see errors like the following in the browser console:

```
Access to fetch at 'https://commerce.example.com/graphql' from origin 'http://localhost:3000' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present
```

## Quick test: Is CORS working?

Section titled “Quick test: Is CORS working?”
Adobe Commerce uses /graphql as the GraphQL endpoint, and this is the primary endpoint that requires CORS configuration. If you already have CORS configured, test it by replacing YOUR_STOREFRONT_URL with your actual frontend URL:

```
1
curl
 
-I
 
-X
 
OPTIONS
 
https://your-commerce-backend.com/graphql
 
\
2
  
-H
 
"Origin: YOUR_STOREFRONT_URL"
 
\
3
  
-H
 
"Access-Control-Request-Method: POST"
```

Look for these headers in the response:

- Access-Control-Allow-Origin: YOUR_STOREFRONT_URL (or * if using a wildcard)
- Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS

If you see these headers with your storefront URL, CORS is configured correctly. If not, follow the setup steps below.

## Quick steps

Section titled “Quick steps”
### Add CORS support

Section titled “Add CORS support”
To add CORS headers to your Adobe Commerce GraphQL endpoints, you have several options:

- **Server configuration**: Configure CORS headers at the web server level ([Nginx](https://enable-cors.org/server_nginx.html) , [Apache](https://enable-cors.org/server_apache.html) )
- **Third-party module**: Use a community module such as [graycore/magento2-cors](https://github.com/graycoreio/magento2-cors)
- **Custom module**: Implement a custom Adobe Commerce module to add CORS headers

Support scope

Third-party modules and custom module implementations are outside the scope of Adobe Commerce support. For production environments, Adobe recommends server-level configuration or same-origin delivery to avoid CORS requirements entirely.

Refer to your chosen implementation’s documentation for specific configuration steps.

### Configure CORS settings

Section titled “Configure CORS settings”
Configure your CORS implementation to allow requests from your storefront domain(s) to your Adobe Commerce GraphQL endpoint.

At minimum, you’ll need to configure:

- **Allowed origins**: Your storefront domain(s) (for example, http://localhost:3000, https://your-storefront.com)
- **Allowed methods**: GET, POST, OPTIONS
- **Allowed headers**: Content-Type, Authorization, X-Requested-With

Refer to your chosen implementation’s documentation for specific configuration steps.

### Test your CORS configuration

Section titled “Test your CORS configuration”
Open your storefront in a browser and check the Network tab in DevTools:

- Look for preflight OPTIONS requests to your GraphQL endpoint
- Verify the response includes headers like: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <your-storefront-url> (or * if using a wildcard) Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization

If configured correctly, your GraphQL requests should succeed without CORS errors.

## Common pitfalls

Section titled “Common pitfalls”
Avoid these common mistakes

**Forgetting to clear cache:** After changing CORS settings, always run bin/magento cache:flush. A stale cache is the primary cause of “it’s not working” reports.

**Using * with credentials:** You cannot use a wildcard * origin when Allow Credentials is enabled. Browsers will block the request.

**Missing the OPTIONS method:** All CORS requests start with an OPTIONS preflight request. If you forget to include OPTIONS in **Allowed Methods**, all CORS requests will fail.

## Next steps

Section titled “Next steps”
If you encounter issues or need detailed configuration guidance, see [CORS Troubleshooting](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/cors-troubleshooting/)

## References

Section titled “References”
- [CORS specification](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) - MDN Web Docs on Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
- [CORS errors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS/Errors) - MDN documentation on common CORS error messages

# CORS Troubleshooting | Adobe Commerce Storefront

**Fonte original:** https://experienceleague.adobe.com/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/cors-troubleshooting

**Coletado em (UTC):** 2026-07-22T14:22:09.070873+00:00

# CORS Troubleshooting

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();

```
1
Access to fetch at 'https://commerce.example.com/graphql' from origin 'http://localhost:3000'
2
has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the
3
requested resource.
```

#### Cause

Section titled “Cause”
CORS headers are not being sent by your Commerce backend. This could mean:

- CORS support is not configured
- The origin is not in the allowed list
- The configuration cache needs to be cleared

#### Solution

Section titled “Solution”
- Verify CORS is configured. See [CORS Setup](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/cors-setup/) if not configured yet.
- Add your storefront origin to the allowed origins list
- Clear the cache: bin/magento cache:flush

### Origin not allowed

Section titled “Origin not allowed”
```
1
Access to fetch at 'https://commerce.example.com/graphql' from origin 'http://localhost:3000'
2
has been blocked by CORS policy: The 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header has a value
3
'https://storefront.example.com' that is not equal to the supplied origin.
```

#### Cause

Section titled “Cause”
The requesting origin is not in the allowed origins list.

#### Solution

Section titled “Solution”
Add the exact origin (including protocol and port) to the Allowed Origins configuration.

### Credentials flag issue

Section titled “Credentials flag issue”
```
1
Access to fetch at 'https://commerce.example.com/graphql' from origin 'http://localhost:3000'
2
has been blocked by CORS policy: The value of the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header in the
3
response must not be the wildcard '*' when the request's credentials mode is 'include'.
```

#### Cause

Section titled “Cause”
You have Allow Credentials enabled but are using * for allowed origins.

#### Solution

Section titled “Solution”
Replace * with specific origins when credentials are required.

### Common issues

Section titled “Common issues”
If you encounter CORS errors after installing adobe-commerce/storefront-compatibility, verify that your CORS implementation is compatible with Adobe Commerce Storefronts. If using the graycore module, ensure v2.x or later is installed.

## Debug checklist

Section titled “Debug checklist”
### Verify CORS is configured

Section titled “Verify CORS is configured”
If using a CORS module, check that it’s installed and enabled:

```
1
# List all enabled modules
2
bin/magento
 
module:status
 
|
 
grep
 
-i
 
cors
```

If using a custom CORS implementation, verify your code is deployed and active.

### Verify CORS configuration

Section titled “Verify CORS configuration”
Check your CORS configuration and confirm:

- Your storefront origin is in the Allowed Origins list
- Origins match exactly (including protocol and port)
- No trailing slashes in origins
- Allowed Methods includes OPTIONS
- Allowed Headers includes all headers your storefront sends

See [CORS Setup](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/cors-setup/) for configuration details.

### Inspect browser network traffic

Section titled “Inspect browser network traffic”
Open DevTools > Network tab and look for:

#### Preflight OPTIONS request

Section titled “Preflight OPTIONS request”
```
1
Request URL: https://commerce.example.com/graphql
2
Request Method: OPTIONS
```

Expected response headers:

```
1
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:3000
2
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS
3
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization
4
Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400
```

#### Actual GraphQL POST request

Section titled “Actual GraphQL POST request”
```
1
Request URL: https://commerce.example.com/graphql
2
Request Method: POST
```

Expected response headers:

```
1
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:3000
2
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```

### Check server logs

Section titled “Check server logs”
If CORS headers are present but requests still fail:

```
1
tail
 
-f
 
var/log/system.log
2
tail
 
-f
 
var/log/exception.log
```

Look for PHP errors, GraphQL exceptions, or module conflicts.

### Clear all caches

Section titled “Clear all caches”
After any configuration changes:

```
1
bin/magento
 
cache:flush
2
bin/magento
 
cache:clean
```

Some CORS configurations may also be cached in Varnish/Fastly if applicable.

## Distinguishing CORS errors from server-side errors

Section titled “Distinguishing CORS errors from server-side errors”
When debugging, it’s important to distinguish CORS policy failures from server-side GraphQL exceptions. Here’s an example of a server-side error that might be mistaken for a CORS issue:

```
1
{
2
  
"message": "Internal server error",
3
  
"extensions": {
4
    
"debugMessage": "Magento\\InventoryConfiguration\\Model\\IsSourceItemManagementAllowedForProductType\\Interceptor::execute(): Argument #1 ($productType) must be of type string, null given"
5
  
}
6
}
```

This indicates a PHP/GraphQL issue (inventory configuration or compatibility) and not a missing Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

## Edge cases and special scenarios

Section titled “Edge cases and special scenarios”
### Docker and containerized environments

Section titled “Docker and containerized environments”
When running Commerce in Docker, you may need to add multiple origin variations:

```
1
http://localhost:3000
2
http://127.0.0.1:3000
3
http://host.docker.internal:3000
```

Docker hostname variations

Docker networking can cause your browser to use different hostnames for the same service, so you need to add all variations.

### Multiple storefronts

Section titled “Multiple storefronts”
For multiple storefronts accessing the same Commerce backend, add each origin separately:

```
1
https://storefront-us.example.com
2
https://storefront-eu.example.com
3
https://storefront-asia.example.com
```

Each storefront is treated as a separate origin and must be explicitly allowed.

## Production best practices

Section titled “Production best practices”
The recommended production approach is to avoid CORS entirely by serving both the storefront and the backend from the same domain using a CDN proxy.

### Same-origin architecture (recommended)

Section titled “Same-origin architecture (recommended)”
Serve both your storefront and Commerce backend from the same domain:

- Storefront: https://example.com → CDN serves static assets
- GraphQL API: https://example.com/graphql → CDN proxies to Commerce backend

This requires configuring your CDN to proxy /graphql requests to your Commerce backend.

**Benefits:**

- No CORS complexity
- Better performance (fewer preflight requests)
- Simpler security model
- Better caching control

**Implementation approaches:**

- Fastly VCL routing: Configure Fastly to route GraphQL requests to your Commerce backend using VCL (Varnish Configuration Language). The VCL detects requests to /graphql and proxies them to your backend origin while serving other requests from your storefront origin.
- Cloudflare Workers / CDN Edge Functions: Use edge functions to route API requests to your backend dynamically.
- Reverse proxy (Nginx/Apache): Configure your web server to proxy /graphql requests to the backend.

**Note:** This approach requires CDN/infrastructure expertise. If you don’t have these resources, use CORS configuration instead.

### CORS configuration

Section titled “CORS configuration”
If you must use different domains (for example, storefront.example.com → commerce.example.com), use CORS configuration. Use specific allowed origins for single production domains, or a wildcard * when you have multiple dynamic preview URLs (such as Edge Delivery Services branch previews).

## References

Section titled “References”
### CORS standards and specifications

Section titled “CORS standards and specifications”
- [CORS specification](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) - MDN Web Docs on Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
- [CORS errors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS/Errors) - MDN documentation on common CORS error messages
- [CORS headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers#cors) - Complete list of CORS-related HTTP headers
- [Preflight requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Preflight_request) - How browsers use OPTIONS requests for CORS

### Adobe Commerce

Section titled “Adobe Commerce”
- [Adobe Commerce CLI commands](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/docs/commerce-operations/configuration-guide/cli/common-cli-commands.html) - Official documentation for Magento CLI commands used in this guide
- [Adobe Commerce GraphQL](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/graphql/) - GraphQL API documentation

### Additional tools and platforms

Section titled “Additional tools and platforms”
- [Composer documentation](https://getcomposer.org/doc/) - PHP dependency manager used for module installation
- [Docker networking](https://docs.docker.com/network/) - Understanding Docker hostname resolution for CORS origins
- [Fastly VCL documentation](https://developer.fastly.com/reference/vcl/) - For implementing same-origin architecture with Fastly CDN routing

# Gated content | Adobe Commerce Storefront

**Fonte original:** https://experienceleague.adobe.com/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/gated-content

**Coletado em (UTC):** 2026-07-22T14:26:53.710180+00:00

---

# Gated content

(function () {
    var KEY = 'sl-recent-searches';
    var MAX = 8;
    var MAX_TERM_LENGTH = 150;

    function load() {
      try {
        var raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || '[]');
        // Validate: must be an array of strings within the length cap.
        if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
        return raw.filter(function (s) {
          return typeof s === 'string' && s.length > 0 && s.length <= MAX_TERM_LENGTH;
        });
      } catch (e) { return []; }
    }

    function save(term) {
      term = term.trim();
      if (term.length < 2 || term.length > MAX_TERM_LENGTH) return;
      var list = load().filter(function (s) { return s !== term; });
      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

    // onClear is passed in from setupRecentSearches so the "Clear all" button
    // can update the shared `panel` reference and show the empty state in-session.
    function buildPanel(inputEl, onClear) {
      var searches = load();
      var panel = document.createElement('div');
      panel.className = 'sl-rs';
      panel.setAttribute('role', 'region');
      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

      var header = document.createElement('div');
      header.className = 'sl-rs__header';

      var label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = 'Recent searches';
      header.appendChild(label);

      if (searches.length) {
        var clearBtn = document.createElement('button');
        clearBtn.className = 'sl-rs__clear';
        clearBtn.textContent = 'Clear all';
        clearBtn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
        clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (onClear) onClear();
        });
        header.appendChild(clearBtn);
      }

      panel.appendChild(header);

      if (searches.length) {
        var chips = document.createElement('div');
        chips.className = 'sl-rs__chips';
        searches.forEach(function (term) {
          var btn = document.createElement('button');
          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');
          btn.textContent = term;
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            inputEl.value = term;
            inputEl.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
            inputEl.focus();
            panel.style.display = 'none';
          });
          chips.appendChild(btn);
        });
        panel.appendChild(chips);
      } else {
        var empty = document.createElement('p');
        empty.className = 'sl-rs__empty';
        empty.textContent = 'Your recent searches will appear here.';
        panel.appendChild(empty);
      }

      return panel;
    }

    // AbortController for the current dialog session. Calling .abort() removes
    // all session listeners in one call, preventing accumulation across opens.
    var sessionAbort = null;

    function setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl) {
      // Append to .dialog-frame, not .pagefind-ui, so Pagefind's DOM
      // re-renders (triggered by the clear button) can't remove our panel.
      var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
      // Guard: skip if frame is missing or the panel is already showing.
      if (!frame || frame.querySelector('.sl-rs')) return;

      // Cancel any leftover listeners from a previous session before attaching
      // new ones. Without this, each dialog open stacks an extra copy of every
      // listener onto the same persistent inputEl and dialog nodes.
      if (sessionAbort) sessionAbort.abort();
      sessionAbort = new AbortController();
      var signal = sessionAbort.signal;

      // Shared panel reference. refreshPanel keeps it current so that
      // syncVisibility, onClear, and the keydown handler all target the live node.
      var panel;

      // Builds a fresh panel, replaces the old one in the DOM, and updates `panel`.
      function refreshPanel(hidden) {
        var next = buildPanel(inputEl, onClear);
        if (hidden) next.style.display = 'none';
        var old = frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
        if (old) old.replaceWith(next);
        else frame.appendChild(next);
        panel = next;
      }

      // Called by the "Clear all" button. Wipes storage, rebuilds to empty state,
      // then immediately syncs visibility so the panel shows/hides correctly
      // based on the current input value without waiting for the next input event.
      function onClear() {
        localStorage.removeItem(KEY);
        refreshPanel(false);
        syncVisibility();
      }

      // Reference panel directly — avoids a DOM query on every keystroke.
      function syncVisibility() {
        panel.style.display = inputEl.value.trim() ? 'none' : '';
      }

      refreshPanel(false); // Initial render.

      // Native input event (typing).
      inputEl.addEventListener('input', syncVisibility, { signal: signal });

      // Pagefind's X button clears the input programmatically without firing
      // a native input event, so we listen for its click separately.
      var pfClear = pagefindEl.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-clear');
      if (pfClear) {
        pfClear.addEventListener('click', function () {
          setTimeout(syncVisibility, 0);
        }, { signal: signal });
      }

      inputEl.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
          // Rebuild so the saved term appears as a chip. Hidden because the
          // input still has text; syncVisibility will show it when cleared.
          refreshPanel(true);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });

      dialog.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        if (e.target.closest('.pagefind-ui__result-link') && inputEl.value.trim()) {
          save(inputEl.value);
        }
      }, { signal: signal });
    }

    function attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog) {
      var inputEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
      var pagefindEl = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');

      if (inputEl && pagefindEl) {
        setupRecentSearches(dialog, inputEl, pagefindEl);
        return;
      }

      // PagefindUI hasn't mounted yet — observe for it with a bounded timeout.
      var inner;
      var innerTimer;
      inner = new MutationObserver(function () {
        // Dialog was closed before Pagefind mounted — bail out cleanly.
        if (!dialog.open) { clearTimeout(innerTimer); inner.disconnect(); return; }
        var inp = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui__search-input');
        var pf = searchDiv.querySelector('.pagefind-ui');
        if (inp && pf) {
          clearTimeout(innerTimer); // Cancel the safety timeout — no longer needed.
          inner.disconnect();
          setupRecentSearches(dialog, inp, pf);
        }
      });
      inner.observe(searchDiv, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      innerTimer = setTimeout(function () { inner.disconnect(); }, 5000);
    }

    function init() {
      // Remove this IIFE's own listener immediately on every call. If setup
      // cannot complete yet, we re-add it below so the next navigation retries.
      // This prevents no-op listeners from accumulating on document: each content
      // swap (View Transitions) re-executes is:inline, creating a new IIFE and a
      // new `init`. Without this pattern, every navigation would leave a stale
      // no-op listener on document even after the dialog guard fires.
      document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', init);

      // #starlight__search is a <div> INSIDE the <dialog>, not a wrapper around it.
      var searchDiv = document.getElementById('starlight__search');
      if (!searchDiv) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      var dialog = searchDiv.closest('dialog');
      if (!dialog) {
        document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init); // Retry on next nav.
        return;
      }

      // Guard against duplicate observer creation across View Transition content
      // swaps. A data attribute on the persistent dialog element survives DOM swaps
      // and prevents a second outer MutationObserver from being attached.
      // No re-add here — setup is permanent once the dialog is found.
      if (dialog.dataset.slRsReady) return;
      dialog.dataset.slRsReady = '1';

      var outer = new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (dialog.open) {
          attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
        } else {
          // Abort all session listeners at once. Panel lives in .dialog-frame.
          if (sessionAbort) { sessionAbort.abort(); sessionAbort = null; }
          var frame = dialog.querySelector('.dialog-frame');
          var panel = frame && frame.querySelector('.sl-rs');
          if (panel) panel.remove();
        }
      });

      outer.observe(dialog, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open'] });

      if (dialog.open) attachToDialog(searchDiv, dialog);
    }

    document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', init);
    init();
  })();
If your site is not managed by Adobe Commerce, you might want to restrict access to certain content, such as videos, images, or pages on your site. This content resides on the edge and cannot be controlled using customer segments or other Commerce functionality. You can restrict access to these non-Commerce assets using gated content.

## Big picture

Section titled “Big picture”
There are several things to know to implement this feature.

- Gated content is displayed only if the customer is logged in and their authentication token is valid. Anonymous users cannot access gated content.
- You must define the gated content. In most cases, you define the path to the gated content in the header document. This file contains a list of URLs that are gated and defines a key/value pair for your custom code to evaluate. (You can also hardcode URLs in your custom code, but this information is easier to maintain in the spreadsheet.) The spreadsheet contains three columns: url - The path to the gated content. Wildcards are supported. key - Any key that you want to use to evaluate whether the content is gated. value - True or other value to be evaluated.
- You must create custom code that evaluates whether access to the content is gated. CDNs typically do not provide the ability to evaluate whether a user is authenticated. As a result, you must implement an auxiliary service, such as Fastly Compute, Amazon Lambda, or Cloudflare workers to perform the evaluation. This code must be able to send an authentication request to Adobe Commerce and process the result. The request is typically a simple GraphQL query, such as the customer query, but you can use any query or mutation that checks if the customer is authenticated.

## Workflow

Section titled “Workflow”
The following diagram illustrates the workflow when gated content is enabled.

Gated content workflow
The shopper requests a page on the storefront. The request is sent to the CDN (Fastly in this case), which then routes it to Edge Delivery Services. Edge Delivery Services returns the requested document with headers defined in the header document. Fastly Compute checks whether the requested page is considered gated content based on the headers returned by Edge Delivery Services or by comparing it with a hardcoded list of gated content. If the header defined in the header document is not present, or if the requested URL is not in the hardcoded gated content list, the request is processed normally.

If the requested page is gated, the Fastly Compute code uses the customer token to construct an authorization request to Adobe Commerce. If the customer is authenticated, the request is allowed to pass through. If the customer is not authenticated, the request is redirected to a fallback page, such as a login page.

## Example implementation

Section titled “Example implementation”
You can [download a sample solution](/developer/commerce/storefront/samples/fastly-compute-sample.zip) that provides an outline of how to implement gated content using Fastly Compute. This sample is based on Fastly’s [Default starter kit for JavaScript](https://www.fastly.com/documentation/solutions/starters/compute-starter-kit-javascript-default/) .

Important

Adobe does not support this example implementation. It is provided as a reference only.

The README provides an overview of the solution and how to install the starter kit. The index.js file contains a Fastly Compute@Edge script that handles incoming HTTP requests and performs user authentication for specific protected URLs.

        return raw.filter(function (s) {

        });

    }

      list.unshift(term);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list.slice(0, MAX)));
      } catch (e) { /* QuotaExceededError or SecurityError — silently skip */ }
    }

      panel.className = 'sl-rs';

      panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Recent searches');

          btn.className = 'sl-rs__chip';
          btn.setAttribute('type', 'button');

**Multistore** enables you to run multiple storefronts from a single codebase and content repository. Each storefront can serve different languages, currencies, regions, or brands while sharing core code and maintaining unified content delivery.

## What is multistore?

Section titled “What is multistore?”
Multistore is useful for:

- **Localization**: Serving different languages and currencies (for example, English/US, French/Canada) from the same site, with localized content and Commerce data.
- **Multiple Brands or Regions**: Operating several brands or regional storefronts, each with their own configuration, but sharing core code and content.

There are two main approaches to multistore:

- **Multiple Domains**: Each domain points to a different commerce backend or configuration, but shares the same code and content.
- **Subfolders (Root Folders)**: A single domain with subfolders (such as /en/, /fr/) for each locale or store. Each subfolder can have its own localized content and Commerce configuration.

**Key features:**

- **Editorial and Commerce Localization**: Editorial content (pages, blocks) and commerce data (products, prices, currencies) are both localized.
- **Automated Translation Tools**: Tools are provided to automate translation of content and manage updates across languages.
- **Configurable Headers**: Storefronts can send different headers to the commerce backend to select the correct store, language, and currency.
- **Store Switcher**: Out-of-the-box UI enables users to switch between stores and locales.
- **Automatic Link Management**: Links are automatically updated to point to the correct localized version as users navigate.

## How it works

Section titled “How it works”
Adobe Commerce uses a [hierarchical structure](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/start/setup/websites-stores-views) to manage multiple stores within a single instance. This structure consists of three levels: websites, stores, and store views. Localization is managed at the store view level, allowing merchants to present the store in different languages and apply the proper currency.

Each store or locale is defined in configuration files, specifying which headers to send to the commerce backend, which content folders to use, and how to structure localized content. The content hierarchy follows [Edge Delivery Services](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/edge-delivery/overview) best practices, emphasizing a single-tier structure.

### Content organization

Section titled “Content organization”
Content is organized primarily by language. US English files should be placed in the en directory of the project root. All other language- and region-specific files should be placed in a directory that is named in the format language-code-region-code (using hyphens). For example, the /en/ directory contains data for the US market, while the /en-ca/ directory contains data for Canada. French content should be placed in directories with names like fr-fr for France and fr-ca for Canada.

- Directory /en/ — English store (Default root language) Directory placeholders/ — Stores JSON files for text and UI components for the English US store. … index — The home page of the English US store. store-switcher — Manages the list of stores and their URL for the English US store.
- Directory /en-ca/ — English Canadian Store Directory placeholders/ — Defines JSON files for text and UI components for the Canadian store. … index — The home page of the English Canadian store. store-switcher — Manages the list of stores and their URL for the Canadian store.

### Store-specific files

Section titled “Store-specific files”
Each store view requires specific files to define the customer experience:

**Store switcher**: Each store view has its own store-switcher document file (called a fragment). This fragment provides the list of stores to select from by language. The store-switcher component renders a button in the footer that opens a modal containing the stores listed in this document.

**Content files**: The content files provide the structure of the pages served to your shoppers. They are located in the store view directories and contain the content for each store view. These files are documents hosted on da.live (Document Authoring environment), SharePoint, or Google Docs that are used to generate the store view pages.

**Placeholders**: JSON files that define reusable variables for text and UI components. Each drop-in component has its own placeholder file—cart.json, checkout.json, pdp.json. These files replace variables in your content files with text values.

**Merchant guidance:** For translating placeholder files, see [Commerce localization tasks](/developer/commerce/storefront/merchants/quick-start/content-localization-commerce-tasks/).

**Developer guidance:** For technical implementation details, see [Labeling and Localizing Drop-In Components](/developer/commerce/storefront/dropins/all/labeling/).

## Prerequisites

Section titled “Prerequisites”
Before implementing multistore functionality, ensure you have:

- Your storefront repository linked to Document Authoring environment (da.live) via Edge Delivery Services
- Access to Adobe Commerce Admin for [store view configuration](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/stores-sales/site-store/store-views)
- Your [Storefront Configuration](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/commerce-configuration/) set up and pointing to the Adobe Commerce instance
- Familiarity with [Authoring and Publishing Content](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/edge-delivery/document-authoring/authoring)
- Understanding of [Storefront Configuration](/developer/commerce/storefront/setup/configuration/commerce-configuration)
- Knowledge of [Adobe Commerce Configuration Scope](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/config/scope-change)

## Implementation walkthrough

Section titled “Implementation walkthrough”
This walkthrough demonstrates the complete process from initial planning to final validation, using a real-world scenario where the Acme brand expands from the United States to the Canadian market with two new locales: Canadian English (en-ca) and Canadian French (fr-ca).

### Verify environment setup

Section titled “Verify environment setup”
Before implementing multistore functionality, confirm your environment is properly configured.

- Verify the code sync bot is installed on your repository. This automatically configures your site’s content pointer to the Document Authoring environment at da.live.
- Verify the config.json file (or Configuration Service) is connected to your Adobe Commerce instance to enable content preview, publishing, and editing.

Environment setup

This verification step is crucial as it ensures you can properly preview and publish content for your new store views.

### Create the content folder structure

Section titled “Create the content folder structure”
Set up the folder structure in your Document Authoring environment to support the new store views.

- Navigate to the connected content folder in da.live.
- Create the Canadian English folder : Select “New folder” Name it en-ca
- Create the Canadian French folder : Select “New folder” Name it fr-ca
- Copy content from the default root folder into each new store view folder: Select all content from the /en/ folder Copy the content Navigate to the en-ca folder and paste Repeat for the fr-ca folder

Folder naming

**Standard format:** Use hyphens for locale folders (en-ca, fr-ca) following the language-code-region-code pattern. This aligns with:

- ISO 639-1 (language codes) and ISO 3166-1 (country codes)
- Web URL conventions
- Adobe/AEM.live best practices

Ensure folder names match exactly with Adobe Commerce store view codes and can be used in web addresses.

### Configure Adobe Commerce store views

Section titled “Configure Adobe Commerce store views”
Create the corresponding store views in Adobe Commerce Admin to match your content folder structure.

- Access Adobe Commerce Admin and navigate to Stores → Settings → All Stores.
- Create the Canadian English store view : Follow the store view creation process Configure as: one website, one store, one store view Set the store view code to match your folder name ( en-ca )
- Create the Canadian French store view : Repeat the process for the French locale Set the store view code to match your folder name ( fr-ca )

Store view codes

The store view codes in Adobe Commerce Admin must exactly match the folder names created in da.live for proper integration.

### Update folder mapping

Section titled “Update folder mapping”
Product Detail Pages (PDP) are mapped to a single document at products/default. When adding a new store view, you must add a corresponding folder mapping for the new URLs using the **Config Service API**.

#### Step 1: Authenticate

Section titled “Step 1: Authenticate”
Go to https://admin.hlx.page/login, then go to your selected IDP login URL, and sign in. Retrieve the auth token from your browser’s cookie storage (available in Developer Tools → Application → Cookies). Use that token to authenticate Admin API requests, with the headers and request format described in the [Config Service setup guide](https://www.aem.live/docs/config-service-setup) and the [Admin API reference](https://www.aem.live/docs/admin.html) .

#### Step 2: Get the current folder configuration

Section titled “Step 2: Get the current folder configuration”
